raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This is component 4 of the DFlash adaptive-verification series. Original implementation and component-only review: https://github.com/jianc99/sglang/pull/4. Integration and full-system results: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46182.

Updated onto upstream `main` (6a319e7b). All applicable pre-commit checks passed on this branch. The GPU tests and benchmark results below were run previously on the original source branch; they have not been rerun after this upstream update. Submission preparation used AI assistance.

---

## Problem

Confidence-scheduled (compact) verification sizes each request's verify window from per-position acceptance probabilities. DSpark drafts get these from a trained confidence head. Draft models without such a head, like DFlash2, have no confidence source, so they cannot use the planner.

## Fix

Add `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator` (python/sglang/srt/speculative/online_acceptance_estimator.py), a logistic model that calibrates itself while serving:

    p_k = sigmoid(slope * x_k + bias_k)

- **Feature.** x_k = logit(q_max) of the temperature-scaled draft distribution at position k. Greedy rows are scored at T = 1, and the value is clamped to +-40. It is computed exactly as -log(sum over the non-max candidates of e^(z - m)), so confident rows are not quantized. The feature scores the draft distribution, not the sampled token, so trimming drafts by it keeps rejection sampling lossless.
- **Model.** One slope is shared by all positions, and each position has its own intercept. They start at 0.5 and -0.2.
- **Learning.** `observe()` labels the accepted drafts and the first rejected one (positions k <= accepted and k < verified) and adds them to the Newton (IRLS) statistics, with weights evaluated at the current coefficients.
- **Refit.** Every 100 calls it solves the arrowhead system (ridge 1e-3) via the Schur complement, damps each update by n / (n + 50), and clears the statistics.
  - A slope step that would make the slope negative is halved until the slope stays positive, at most 8 times, and dropped only if it still crosses zero. The intercepts take their Newton step given the slope step actually taken.
  - This backtracking is its own commit, 874094430, on top of the estimator commit 17ed303ce. 17ed303ce dropped every such step. From an overconfident fit the predictions saturate, the damped step overshoots past zero round after round, and the slope never moved: started at 3.0 on drafts generated with slope 1.0, it stayed at 3.0, and from the default 0.5 on drafts whose feature carries almost no signal it could stay at 0.5. With backtracking, within ten refits the slope reaches 0.96 in the first case and 0 to 0.06 in the second (generating slope 0 or 0.03). Refits whose full step keeps the slope positive are unchanged.
  - Non-finite steps are dropped.

Interface:
- `feature_from_scores(scores [bs, K, n_cand], temperatures) -> x [bs, K]`
- `predict(x) -> p [bs, K]`, with no state change
- `feature_and_predict(scores, temperatures) -> (x, p)`, both in one kernel launch
- `observe(x, num_verified, num_accepted)`
  - num_verified excludes the anchor; num_accepted excludes the bonus token.
  - Padding rows pass num_verified = 0 and are never read.
  - Call it once per real verify step, never from warmup or dummy forwards.

Two Triton kernels in python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/acceptance_estimator.py compute the feature (optionally with the prediction) and the accumulate/refit. Both are registered in the kernel inventory. The refit counter is a device tensor, the refit interval is a runtime kernel argument, and the coefficients are updated in place. As a result:
- No call synchronizes with the host, so the estimator works with overlap scheduling.
- The whole step can be captured in a CUDA graph.
- A single program applies each update, backtracking included, so TP ranks that see the same inputs keep bit-identical coefficients.

## Effect

No behavior change on its own: nothing in this PR calls the estimator. Its only caller is https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46190, which uses it as the confidence source for confidence-scheduled verification of DFLASH drafts, so the two should be reviewed together. This PR has no end-to-end speed numbers; those are in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46190.

Offline, the estimator was replayed in order over recorded static DFlash2 traces of Qwen3.8-27B (block 8, 1.8M to 2.9M draft positions each). AUC of the predicted survival against acceptance:

| Trace | Estimator | Raw q_max product |
|---|---|---|
| T = 1, c64 | 0.898 | 0.886 |
| T = 1, c128 | 0.898 | 0.886 |
| T = 0, c64 | 0.921 | 0.920 |
| T = 0, c128 | 0.919 | 0.918 |

These AUCs were measured on 17ed303ce, before the backtracking in 874094430.

Cost on GB300, K = 7, 16 candidates, measured on 17ed303ce:

| | bs <= 128 | bs = 512 |
|---|---|---|
| Fused feature + predict, then observe: GPU time in a CUDA graph | 6-8 us | 10 us |
| Separate kernels: GPU time in a CUDA graph | 10 us | 14 us |
| Fused step: host time eager | 55-56 us | 56 us |
| Separate step: host time eager | 85-89 us | 87 us |

The backtracking in 874094430 adds at most 0.1 us of GPU time to `observe()` (bs 1 to 512, K = 7 and 16, refit on every call or every 100 calls).

## Tests

test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_online_acceptance_estimator.py (CUDA, about 30 s; also registered for the ROCm nightly kernel suite) covers:
- the feature kernel against a float64 reference: dtypes, strides, multi-block candidate rows, ties, clamp and greedy rows;
- the fused feature + predict path against the separate calls;
- observation-rule edge cases;
- padding rows, which leave the estimator bit-identical;
- a float64 reference of the full IRLS round over hundreds of steps, with coefficients matching to 1e-4, including batches that span the kernel's request blocks;
- refit interval and statistics reset;
- slope steps that cross zero: backtracked, or dropped when they still cross it after 8 halvings, and a saturated fit started at slope 3.0 that ends within 0.15 of the generating slope 1.0, where dropping the steps leaves it at 3.0;
- empty batches;
- no host synchronization (`torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`);
- CUDA graph replay matching eager bit-for-bit across refits.

compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and initcheck, run on 17ed303ce before the backtracking, report no device-side errors from these kernels. The only memcheck errors are host API errors raised while flashinfer is imported.

## Related upstream work

sgl-project/sglang#44866 (draft) adds an online acceptance estimator for DSpark's confidence-scheduled verification. It uses the same module path (`srt/speculative/online_acceptance_estimator.py`), the same kernel file (`kernels/ops/speculative/acceptance_estimator.py`) and the same class name, `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator`, so the two cannot both land as they are.

How they differ:
- Model: both score `sigmoid(slope * logit(q_max) + intercept[position])`.
- Fit: sgl-project/sglang#44866 bins observations by (position, feature bin, label) with a decayed history and runs several Newton iterations with a batched line search every 100 steps. This PR keeps exact per-observation IRLS statistics for the round and takes one damped Newton step, with the slope backtracking above.
- Wiring: sgl-project/sglang#44866 wires DSPARK (a `--speculative-dspark-confidence-source` argument, with the trained head used when present) and also changes compact padding rows to a point mass. This PR has no caller; DFLASH uses it through https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46190.

What to do: if sgl-project/sglang#44866 lands first, drop this PR and move https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46190 onto its estimator. The DFLASH wiring needs a feature and a prediction computed inside the draft CUDA graph and one observe call per real verify step, with no host synchronization, so its estimator has to keep that contract.

detail.title: [Feat] spec: online acceptance estimator for drafts without a confidence head

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,309 @@
+"""Kernels for the online draft acceptance estimator.
+
+``max_log_odds`` turns draft scores into the estimator's feature, the log-odds
+of the most likely draft token, and optionally the logistic prediction from it.
+``observe_acceptance`` folds verified drafts into the per-round Newton (IRLS)
+statistics and, every ``refit_interval`` calls, refits the logistic
+coefficients in place. Both read their state from device tensors only, so they
+never synchronize with the host and can be captured in a CUDA graph.
+"""
+
+from typing import Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+# Columns of the per-position statistics: the X^T W X arrowhead entries a, b, c,
+# the X^T r entries g0, g1, and the observation count n.
+NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS = 6
+# A refit halves a slope step that would make the slope non-positive at most
+# this many times before dropping it.
+_MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS = 8
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _max_log_odds_kernel(
+    scores_ptr,
+    stride_req,
+    stride_pos,
+    stride_cand,
+    temperatures_ptr,
+    temperatures_stride,
+    slope_ptr,
+    intercepts_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    probs_ptr,
+    num_positions,
+    num_candidates,
+    MAX_LOG_ODDS: tl.constexpr,
+    WITH_PROBS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    req = row // num_positions
+    pos = row % num_positions
+
+    # Rows with a non-positive temperature are greedy; score them at T = 1.
+    temperature = tl.load(temperatures_ptr + req * temperatures_stride).to(tl.float32)
+    temperature = tl.where(temperature > 0.0, temperature, 1.0)
+
+    row_ptr = scores_ptr + req.to(tl.int64) * stride_req + pos.to(tl.int64) * stride_pos
+
+    # logit(q_max) = log(q_max / (1 - q_max)) = -log(sum_{z != argmax} e^(z - m)),
+    # with m the max score. Track the running max and the sum over every other
+    # candidate directly, so confident rows keep their precision instead of
+    # cancelling in (sum_z e^(z - m)) - 1.
+    run_max = float("-inf")
+    run_rest = 0.0
+    for start in range(0, num_candidates, BLOCK_N):
+        offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+        mask = offs < num_candidates
+        s = tl.load(row_ptr + offs * stride_cand, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(
+            tl.float32
+        )
+        s = s / temperature
+        blk_max = tl.max(s, axis=0)
+        # Exclude exactly one instance of the block max; ties stay in the rest.
+        blk_arg = tl.min(tl.where(s == blk_max, offs, num_candidates), axis=0)
+        e = tl.where((s > float("-inf")) & (offs != blk_arg), tl.exp(s - blk_max), 0.0)
+        blk_rest = tl.sum(e, axis=0)
+        # Merge the block into the running pair; the smaller max joins the rest.
+        rest_new_max = blk_rest + (run_rest + 1.0) * tl.exp(run_max - blk_max)
+        rest_old_max = run_rest + tl.where(
+            blk_max > float("-inf"), (blk_rest + 1.0) * tl.exp(blk_max - run_max), 0.0
+        )
+        run_rest = tl.where(blk_max > run_max, rest_new_max, rest_old_max)
+        run_max = tl.maximum(run_max, blk_max)
+
+    feature = tl.where(run_rest > 0.0, -tl.log(run_rest), MAX_LOG_ODDS)
+    feature = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(feature, -MAX_LOG_ODDS), MAX_LOG_ODDS)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + row, feature)
+    if WITH_PROBS:
+        bias = tl.load(intercepts_ptr + pos)
+        tl.store(probs_ptr + row, tl.sigmoid(tl.load(slope_ptr) * feature + bias))
+
+
+def max_log_odds(
+    scores: torch.Tensor,
+    temperatures: torch.Tensor,
+    clamp: float,
+    slope: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    intercepts: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Log-odds of the most likely candidate of each temperature-scaled row.
+
+    scores: [bs, num_positions, num_candidates] logits; temperatures: one per
+    request (any shape with bs elements). Returns the float32 log-odds
+    [bs, num_positions], clamped to +-clamp, and, when the float32 logistic
+    coefficients slope [1] and intercepts [num_positions] are given, the
+    probabilities sigmoid(slope * x + intercepts[k]) from the same launch
+    (otherwise None).
+
+    One program handles one row and walks its candidates in blocks, so the
+    kernel is sized for candidate lists; a full-vocabulary row runs serially.
+    """
+    bs, num_positions, num_candidates = scores.shape
+    temperatures = temperatures.reshape(-1)
+    assert temperatures.numel() == bs, (temperatures.shape, scores.shape)
+    with_probs = slope is not None
+    assert with_probs == (intercepts is not None)
+    if with_probs:
+        assert slope.numel() == 1 and intercepts.shape == (num_positions,)
+        assert slope.dtype == intercepts.dtype == torch.float32
+    out = torch.empty((bs, num_positions), dtype=torch.float32, device=scores.device)
+    probs = torch.empty_like(out) if with_probs else None
+    if out.numel() == 0:
+        return out, probs
+    block_n = min(triton.next_power_of_2(num_candidates), 4096)
+    _max_log_odds_kernel[(bs * num_positions,)](
+        scores,
+        scores.stride(0),
+        scores.stride(1),
+        scores.stride(2),
+        temperatures,
+        temperatures.stride(0),
+        slope if with_probs else out,
+        intercepts if with_probs else out,
+        out,
+        probs if with_probs else out,
+        num_positions,
+        num_candidates,
+        MAX_LOG_ODDS=clamp,
+        WITH_PROBS=with_probs,
+        BLOCK_N=block_n,
+        num_warps=1 if block_n <= 256 else 4,
+    )
+    return out, probs
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_reqs", "refit_interval"])
+def _observe_acceptance_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    x_stride_req,
+    x_stride_pos,
+    num_verified_ptr,
+    num_accepted_ptr,
+    slope_ptr,
+    intercepts_ptr,
+    stats_ptr,
+    num_calls_ptr,
+    num_reqs,
+    refit_interval,
+    NUM_POSITIONS: tl.constexpr,
+    L2: tl.constexpr,
+    DAMPING: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_STATS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    k_mask = k < NUM_POSITIONS
+    slope = tl.load(slope_ptr)
+    bias = tl.load(intercepts_ptr + k, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+
+    # This call's contribution to the normal equations. Observation i at
+    # position k has design row [x_i, e_k], IRLS weight w_i = p_i (1 - p_i) and
+    # residual y_i - p_i, so it adds w x^2 to a, w x to b_k, w to c_k, r x to
+    # g0 and r to g1_k. a and g0 are kept per position and summed at refit.
+    a_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    b_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    c_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    g0_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    g1_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    n_k = tl.zeros([BLOCK_K], dtype=tl.float32)
+    for start in range(0, num_reqs, BLOCK_R):
+        r = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+        r_mask = r < num_reqs
+        verified = tl.load(num_verified_ptr + r, mask=r_mask, other=0)
+        accepted = tl.load(num_accepted_ptr + r, mask=r_mask, other=0)
+        # The accepted drafts and the first rejected one are observed; drafts
+        # after the first rejection, or never verified, carry no label.
+        observed = (
+            r_mask[:, None]
+            & k_mask[None, :]
+            & (k[None, :] <= accepted[:, None])
+            & (k[None, :] < verified[:, None])
+        )
+        x = tl.load(
+            x_ptr + r.to(tl.int64)[:, None] * x_stride_req + k[None, :] * x_stride_pos,
+            mask=observed,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        p = tl.sigmoid(slope * x + bias[None, :])
+        label = tl.where(k[None, :] < accepted[:, None], 1.0, 0.0)
+        w = tl.where(observed, p * (1.0 - p), 0.0)
+        resid = tl.where(observed, label - p, 0.0)
+        a_k += tl.sum(w * x * x, axis=0)
+        b_k += tl.sum(w * x, axis=0)
+        c_k += tl.sum(w, axis=0)
+        g0_k += tl.sum(resid * x, axis=0)
+        g1_k += tl.sum(resid, axis=0)
+        n_k += tl.sum(observed.to(tl.float32), axis=0)
+
+    s_ptr = stats_ptr + k * NUM_STATS
+    a_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 0, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    b_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 1, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    c_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 2, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    g0_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 3, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    g1_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 4, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    n_k += tl.load(s_ptr + 5, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+
+    num_calls = tl.load(num_calls_ptr) + 1
+    # Every warp must read the state before any warp overwrites it below, or a
+    # late warp could see the new call count and disagree on the refit.
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    refit = num_calls >= refit_interval
+    if refit:
+        # One damped Newton step on the round's statistics: solve the arrowhead
+        # system (X^T W X + L2 I) [d_slope, d_bias_0 .. d_bias_n-1] = X^T r,
+        #   [ a+L2  b_0      ...  b_n-1     ] [ d_slope    ]   [ g0     ]
+        #   [ b_0   c_0+L2                  ] [ d_bias_0   ] = [ g1_0   ]
+        #   [ ...          ...              ] [ ...        ]   [ ...    ]
+        #   [ b_n-1             c_n-1+L2    ] [ d_bias_n-1 ]   [ g1_n-1 ]
+        # by eliminating the diagonal block (Schur complement on the slope).
+        c_reg = tl.where(k_mask, c_k + L2, 1.0)
+        a = tl.sum(a_k, axis=0) + L2
+        g0 = tl.sum(g0_k, axis=0)
+        step_slope = (g0 - tl.sum(b_k * g1_k / c_reg, axis=0)) / (
+            a - tl.sum(b_k * b_k / c_reg, axis=0)
+        )
+        # The slope learns from every position, so it is damped by the round's
+        # total observation count; each intercept by its own.
+        total_n = tl.sum(n_k, axis=0)
+        step_slope *= total_n / (total_n + DAMPING)
+        # From an overconfident fit the predictions saturate, the curvature is
+        # small and the step overshoots past zero. Backtrack: halve the step
+        # until the slope stays positive. Drop non-finite steps and steps that
+        # still cross zero after MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS halvings.
+        for _ in tl.static_range(MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS):
+            step_slope = tl.where(
+                slope + step_slope > 0.0, step_slope, step_slope * 0.5
+            )
+        valid = (tl.abs(step_slope) < float("inf")) & (slope + step_slope > 0.0)
+        step_slope = tl.where(valid, step_slope, 0.0)
+        step_bias = (g1_k - b_k * step_slope) / c_reg
+        step_bias *= n_k / (n_k + DAMPING)
+        step_bias = tl.where(tl.abs(step_bias) < float("inf"), step_bias, 0.0)
+        tl.store(slope_ptr, slope + step_slope)
+        tl.store(intercepts_ptr + k, bias + step_bias, mask=k_mask)
+
+    # A refit consumes the round: the next one starts from clean statistics.
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 0, tl.where(refit, 0.0, a_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 1, tl.where(refit, 0.0, b_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 2, tl.where(refit, 0.0, c_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 3, tl.where(refit, 0.0, g0_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 4, tl.where(refit, 0.0, g1_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(s_ptr + 5, tl.where(refit, 0.0, n_k), mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(num_calls_ptr, tl.where(refit, 0, num_calls))
+
+
+def observe_acceptance(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    num_verified: torch.Tensor,
+    num_accepted: torch.Tensor,
+    slope: torch.Tensor,
+    intercepts: torch.Tensor,
+    stats: torch.Tensor,
+    num_calls: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    refit_interval: int,
+    l2: float,
+    damping: float,
+    block_reqs: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Accumulate one batch of verified drafts and refit when a round ends.
+
+    x: float [bs, K] features the drafts were scored with; num_verified /
+    num_accepted: int [bs] drafts the target verified / accepted per request.
+    slope [1], intercepts [K], stats [K, NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS] and the int32
+    call counter num_calls [1] are updated in place by a single program, so the
+    result is deterministic.
+    """
+    num_reqs, num_positions = x.shape
+    assert intercepts.shape == (num_positions,), (intercepts.shape, x.shape)
+    assert (
+        stats.shape == (num_positions, NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS) and stats.is_contiguous()

+        num_calls,
+        num_reqs,
+        refit_interval,
+        NUM_POSITIONS=num_positions,
+        L2=l2,
+        DAMPING=damping,
+        MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS=_MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS,
+        NUM_STATS=NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS,
+        BLOCK_R=block_reqs,

+"""Online per-position acceptance estimator for drafts without a confidence head.
+
+Confidence-scheduled verification needs the probability that each draft token
+is accepted given that every earlier one was. A draft model without a trained
+confidence head gets it from a logistic model calibrated while serving:
+
+    p_k = sigmoid(slope * x_k + bias_k)
+
+where x_k = logit(q_max) is the log-odds of the most likely token of the draft
+distribution at position k, slope is shared by all positions and bias_k is
+per position. The feature scores the draft distribution, not the sampled
+token, so trimming drafts by it never conditions on the trimmed token and
+rejection sampling stays lossless.
+
+The coefficients are refit by one damped Newton (IRLS) step every
+``refit_interval`` observations. Everything stays on the device and no call
+synchronizes with the host, so the estimator runs under overlap scheduling and
+inside CUDA graphs. All state updates are deterministic, so ranks that observe
+identical inputs keep identical coefficients.
+"""
+
+from typing import Tuple
+
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.acceptance_estimator import (
+    NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS,
+    max_log_odds,
+    observe_acceptance,
+)
+
+# The feature log(q / (1 - q)) is infinite for a row with all of its mass on one
+# token; clamp it symmetrically.
+_MAX_LOG_ODDS = 40.0
+# Cold-start coefficients. Log-loss is flat near the optimum, so one starting
+# point serves typical draft models and the first refits replace it.
+_INIT_SLOPE = 0.5
+_INIT_BIAS = -0.2
+# Newton steps are damped by n / (n + _DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS): a round with this
+# many observations moves a coefficient half of a full step, so data-poor
+# positions keep learning, only slowly.
+_DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS = 50.0
+# Ridge on the Newton solve.
+_L2 = 1e-3
+# Rows of requests the observe kernel processes per iteration.
+_MAX_BLOCK_REQS = 256
+
+
+class OnlineAcceptanceEstimator:
+    """Per-position conditional acceptance probabilities from draft confidence.
+
+    Per verify step the caller:
+    1. ``feature_from_scores`` on the draft scores of each position,
+    2. ``predict`` to get the conditional acceptance probabilities,
+    3. after verification, ``observe`` with the same features and the verify
+       outcome.
+    ``feature_and_predict`` does steps 1 and 2 in one kernel launch.
+    ``observe`` evaluates the Newton weights at the current coefficients, so it
+    may run before or after the next step's ``predict``.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_positions: int,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        refit_interval: int = 100,
+    ) -> None:
+        assert num_positions > 0 and max_num_reqs > 0 and refit_interval > 0
+        self.num_positions = num_positions
+        self.refit_interval = refit_interval
+        self._block_reqs = min(triton.next_power_of_2(max_num_reqs), _MAX_BLOCK_REQS)
+        # Coefficients are updated in place, so CUDA graphs that read them stay
+        # valid across refits.
+        self.slope = torch.full((1,), _INIT_SLOPE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        self.intercepts = torch.full(
+            (num_positions,), _INIT_BIAS, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+        )
+        # Per-round Newton statistics per position, cleared at every refit.
+        self._stats = torch.zeros(
+            (num_positions, NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS), dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+        )
+        # observe() calls since the last refit.
+        self._num_calls = torch.zeros((1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def feature_from_scores(
+        self, scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """scores [bs, num_positions, num_candidates]: the draft logits each
+        position sampled from; temperatures: per request, greedy rows <= 0.
+        Returns logit(q_max) of the temperature-scaled rows, float32
+        [bs, num_positions]."""
+        assert scores.dim() == 3 and scores.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return max_log_odds(scores, temperatures, _MAX_LOG_ODDS)[0]
+
+    def feature_and_predict(
+        self, scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """``feature_from_scores`` and ``predict`` fused into one kernel launch.
+        Returns the features and the conditional acceptance probabilities, both
+        float32 [bs, num_positions]. Does not change any state."""
+        assert scores.dim() == 3 and scores.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return max_log_odds(
+            scores, temperatures, _MAX_LOG_ODDS, self.slope, self.intercepts
+        )
+
+    def predict(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Conditional acceptance probability of each draft position, float32
+        [bs, num_positions]. Does not change any state."""
+        assert x.dim() == 2 and x.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return torch.sigmoid(torch.addcmul(self.intercepts, x.float(), self.slope))
+
+    def observe(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        num_verified: torch.Tensor,
+        num_accepted: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Learn from one verify step.
+
+        x: the features the verified drafts were predicted with, [bs,
+        num_positions]; num_verified: draft tokens the target verified per
+        request, the anchor excluded; num_accepted: how many of them it
+        accepted, the bonus token excluded. Positions up to and including the
+        first rejection are observed, labelled by whether they were accepted.
+        Rows with num_verified = 0 contribute nothing and their features are
+        not read, so padding rows must pass 0. Every ``refit_interval``-th
+        call refits the coefficients and starts a new round.
+
+        This updates the estimator, so run it (or replay a graph that captured
+        it) exactly once per real verify step, never in warmup or dummy
+        forwards.
+        """
+        assert x.dim() == 2 and x.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        assert num_verified.numel() == num_accepted.numel() == x.shape[0]
+        observe_acceptance(
+            x,
+            num_verified.reshape(-1).contiguous(),
+            num_accepted.reshape(-1).contiguous(),
+            self.slope,
+            self.intercepts,
+            self._stats,
+            self._num_calls,
+            refit_interval=self.refit_interval,
+            l2=_L2,
+            damping=_DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS,
+            block_reqs=self._block_reqs,
+        )

+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.speculative.online_acceptance_estimator import OnlineAcceptanceEstimator
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase

+_MAX_LOG_ODDS = 40.0
+_INIT_SLOPE = 0.5
+_INIT_BIAS = -0.2
+_DAMPING = 50.0
+_L2 = 1e-3
+_MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS = 8
+
+
+def _ref_feature(scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """logit(q_max) of the temperature-scaled rows, in float64."""
+    temps = temperatures.reshape(-1).double()
+    temps = torch.where(temps > 0, temps, torch.ones_like(temps))
+    s = scores.double() / temps[:, None, None]
+    top, arg = s.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    rest = torch.exp(s - top).scatter(-1, arg, 0.0).sum(dim=-1)
+    return (-torch.log(rest)).clamp(-_MAX_LOG_ODDS, _MAX_LOG_ODDS)
+
+
+class _RefEstimator:
+    """Float64 reference of the estimator round: observation rule, IRLS
+    statistics, damped Newton refit and the reset after every refit."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_positions: int,
+        refit_interval: int,
+        init_slope: float = _INIT_SLOPE,
+        max_slope_halvings: int = _MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS,
+    ):
+        self.k = num_positions
+        self.refit_interval = refit_interval
+        self.max_slope_halvings = max_slope_halvings
+        self.slope = torch.tensor(init_slope, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.bias = torch.full((num_positions,), _INIT_BIAS, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.stats = torch.zeros(num_positions, 6, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def predict(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.sigmoid(self.slope * x.double() + self.bias)
+
+    def observe(self, x, num_verified, num_accepted):
+        x = x.double().cpu()
+        verified = num_verified.cpu().long()[:, None]
+        accepted = num_accepted.cpu().long()[:, None]
+        pos = torch.arange(self.k)[None, :]
+        observed = (pos <= accepted) & (pos < verified)
+        label = (pos < accepted).double()
+        p = self.predict(x)
+        w = torch.where(observed, p * (1 - p), 0.0)
+        r = torch.where(observed, label - p, 0.0)
+        x = torch.where(observed, x, 0.0)
+        self.stats += torch.stack(
+            [
+                (w * x * x).sum(0),
+                (w * x).sum(0),
+                w.sum(0),
+                (r * x).sum(0),
+                r.sum(0),
+                observed.double().sum(0),
+            ],
+            dim=1,
+        )
+        self.calls += 1
+        if self.calls >= self.refit_interval:
+            self._refit()
+
+    def _refit(self):
+        a, b, c, g0, g1, n = self.stats.unbind(1)
+        # Dense solve of (X^T W X + L2 I) d = X^T r for the slope step.
+        hess = torch.zeros(self.k + 1, self.k + 1, dtype=torch.float64)
+        hess[0, 0] = a.sum()
+        hess[0, 1:] = b
+        hess[1:, 0] = b
+        hess[1:, 1:] = torch.diag(c)
+        hess += _L2 * torch.eye(self.k + 1, dtype=torch.float64)
+        grad = torch.cat([g0.sum()[None], g1])
+        step_slope = torch.linalg.solve(hess, grad)[0]
+        step_slope = step_slope * n.sum() / (n.sum() + _DAMPING)
+        # Backtrack until the slope stays positive, else drop the step.
+        for _ in range(self.max_slope_halvings):
+            if self.slope + step_slope > 0:
+                break
+            step_slope = step_slope / 2
+        if not torch.isfinite(step_slope) or self.slope + step_slope <= 0:
+            step_slope = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.float64)
+        # Intercepts: exact Newton step given the (damped) slope step, damped.
+        step_bias = (g1 - b * step_slope) / (c + _L2) * n / (n + _DAMPING)
+        step_bias = torch.where(torch.isfinite(step_bias), step_bias, 0.0)
+        self.slope = self.slope + step_slope
+        self.bias = self.bias + step_bias
+        self.stats.zero_()
+        self.calls = 0
+
+
+def _random_step(gen, bs, k, true_slope, true_bias, device):
+    """One verify step of synthetic drafts: features, then a verify outcome
+    drawn from the true logistic model, with some requests verifying fewer than
+    k drafts."""
+    x = (torch.randn(bs, k, generator=gen) * 3.0 + 2.0).clamp(
+        -_MAX_LOG_ODDS, _MAX_LOG_ODDS
+    )
+    p = torch.sigmoid(true_slope * x + true_bias)
+    hits = (torch.rand(bs, k, generator=gen) < p).int()
+    leading = torch.cumprod(hits, dim=1).sum(dim=1)
+    verified = torch.randint(0, k + 1, (bs,), generator=gen)
+    verified = torch.where(torch.rand(bs, generator=gen) < 0.7, k, verified)
+    accepted = torch.minimum(leading, verified)
+    return (
+        x.to(device),
+        verified.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        accepted.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+    )
+

+    def test_refit_interval_and_reset(self):
+        k = 4

+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(2)

+                self.assertGreater(est._stats[:, 5].sum().item(), 0)
+                self.assertEqual(est._num_calls.item(), call)

+    def test_slope_step_backtracks_to_stay_positive(self):
+        k = 2
+        # Confident drafts are always rejected, unsure ones always accepted, so
+        # the full Newton step points to a negative slope.
+        x = torch.tensor([[8.0, 8.0]] * 64 + [[-8.0, -8.0]] * 64, device=self.device)
+        verified = torch.full((128,), 2, device=self.device)
+        accepted = torch.tensor([0] * 64 + [2] * 64, device=self.device)
+        # From 0.5 the step is halved until the slope stays positive. From 1e-4
+        # it still crosses zero after every allowed halving and is dropped.
+        for init_slope, slope_moves in [(0.5, True), (1e-4, False)]:
+            est = self._estimator(k=k, refit_interval=1)
+            est.slope.fill_(init_slope)
+            ref = _RefEstimator(k, refit_interval=1, init_slope=est.slope.item())
+            before = est.slope.clone()
+            est.observe(x, verified, accepted)
+            ref.observe(x, verified, accepted)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                est.slope.cpu().double()[0], ref.slope, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5
+            )
+            # The intercepts take the Newton step given the slope step taken.
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                est.intercepts.cpu().double(), ref.bias, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4
+            )
+            if slope_moves:
+                self.assertGreater(est.slope.item(), 0.0)
+                self.assertLess(est.slope.item(), init_slope)
+            else:
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(est.slope, before))
+            self.assertFalse(
+                torch.equal(est.intercepts.cpu(), torch.full((k,), _INIT_BIAS))
+            )

+    def test_saturated_slope_keeps_moving(self):
+        # An overconfident slope saturates the predictions: the curvature is
+        # small and every full Newton step crosses zero. Dropping those steps
+        # pins the slope; backtracking brings it to the generating model.
+        k, bs, refit_interval, rounds = 7, 128, 4, 10
+        init_slope, true_slope = 3.0, 1.0
+        true_bias = torch.linspace(0.6, -0.6, k)
+        est = self._estimator(k=k, max_num_reqs=bs, refit_interval=refit_interval)
+        est.slope.fill_(init_slope)
+        ref = _RefEstimator(k, refit_interval, init_slope=init_slope)
+        dropped = _RefEstimator(
+            k, refit_interval, init_slope=init_slope, max_slope_halvings=0
+        )
+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(6)
+        for _ in range(rounds * refit_interval):
+            x, verified, accepted = _random_step(
+                gen, bs, k, true_slope, true_bias, self.device
+            )
+            for e in (est, ref, dropped):
+                e.observe(x, verified, accepted)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                est.slope.cpu().double()[0], ref.slope, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                est.intercepts.cpu().double(), ref.bias, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(dropped.slope.item(), init_slope)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(est.slope.item(), true_slope, delta=0.15)

+    def test_no_host_sync(self):
+        k = 7
+        est = self._estimator(k=k, refit_interval=2)
+        scores = torch.randn(16, k, 16, device=self.device)
+        temps = torch.ones(16, 1, device=self.device)
+        verified = torch.full((16,), k, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+        accepted = torch.randint(0, k + 1, (16,), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+        # Compile the kernels first.
+        est.observe(est.feature_from_scores(scores, temps), verified, accepted)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+        try:
+            for _ in range(3):  # crosses a refit
+                x = est.feature_from_scores(scores, temps)
+                est.predict(x)
+                est.feature_and_predict(scores, temps)
+                est.observe(x, verified, accepted)
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("default")

+    def test_cuda_graph_replay_matches_eager(self):
+        k, bs, steps = 7, 48, 230
+        true_bias = torch.linspace(0.6, -0.6, k)
+        eager = self._estimator(k=k, max_num_reqs=bs, refit_interval=100)
+        graphed = self._estimator(k=k, max_num_reqs=bs, refit_interval=100)
+        scores = torch.zeros(bs, k, 16, device=self.device)
+        temps = torch.ones(bs, device=self.device)
+        verified = torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+        accepted = torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device)
+
+        def body(est):
+            x, fused_prob = est.feature_and_predict(scores, temps)
+            prob = est.predict(est.feature_from_scores(scores, temps))
+            est.observe(x, verified, accepted)
+            return prob, fused_prob
+
+        warm = self._estimator(k=k, max_num_reqs=bs)
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            body(warm)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            graph_probs = body(graphed)
+
+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(3)
+        for _ in range(steps):
+            x, v, a = _random_step(gen, bs, k, 1.0, true_bias, self.device)
+            # Two-candidate rows [x, 0]: their log-odds feature is |x|.
+            scores.zero_()
+            scores[:, :, 0] = x
+            scores[:, :, 1:] = float("-inf")
+            scores[:, :, 1] = 0.0
+            verified.copy_(v)
+            accepted.copy_(a)
+            graph.replay()
+            for graph_prob, eager_prob in zip(graph_probs, body(eager)):
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(graph_prob, eager_prob))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(graphed.slope, eager.slope))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(graphed.intercepts, eager.intercepts))
+        self.assertNotEqual(eager.slope.item(), _INIT_SLOPE)
